words.enDefinition: the letter grade just below a straight A, worth 3.7 points

examples.en: I finished organic chemistry with an A minus, my best science grade so far.
examples.zh: 有机化学我最终拿了「A减」，是目前为止最好的一门理科成绩。

examples.en: One A minus in first year will not hurt your cumulative GPA much.
examples.zh: 大一拿一个「A减」对你的累计绩点影响不大。

collocations: an A minus in the course
rounded up to an A minus

words.enDefinition: a letter grade above a B, usually worth 3.3 points

examples.en: A B plus in statistics still keeps my major GPA above 3.5.
examples.zh: 统计课拿「B加」仍能让我的专业课绩点保持在3.5以上。

examples.en: The syllabus says 87 to 89 counts as a B plus.
examples.zh: 课程大纲写着87到89分算作「B加」。

collocations: just short of a B plus

words.enDefinition: a letter grade below a B, worth about 2.7 points

examples.en: That B minus in calculus dropped my semester GPA to 3.1.
examples.zh: 微积分那个「B减」把我的学期绩点拉到了3.1。

examples.en: My advisor said one B minus will not sink my graduate applications.
examples.zh: 导师说一个「B减」不至于毁掉我的研究生申请。

words.enDefinition: a middling letter grade, usually worth 2.3 points

examples.en: A C plus in orgo is survivable if the rest of your grades are strong.
examples.zh: 如果其他成绩够强，有机化学拿个「C加」也还能接受。

examples.en: Graduate admissions committees rarely reject an application over a single C plus.
examples.zh: 研究生招生委员会很少会因为一个「C加」就拒掉申请。

collocations: a C plus on the midterm

words.enDefinition: a barely passing letter grade that pulls your GPA down

examples.en: The department requires a C minus or higher to move into the next course.
examples.zh: 系里要求「C减」或更高才能进入下一门课。

examples.en: That C minus in physics is the grade I need to retake.
examples.zh: 物理那个「C减」就是我要重修的成绩。

collocations: repeat the course after a C minus

words.enDefinition: all A grades in every course for a term or year

examples.en: She pulled off straight A's while working twenty hours a week.
examples.zh: 她每周打工二十小时还做到了「全A」。

examples.en: Two semesters of straight A's lifted my cumulative GPA back above 3.7.
examples.zh: 两个学期的「全A」把我的累计绩点重新拉回3.7以上。

words.enDefinition: a high grade needing little effort, or such a class

examples.en: Everyone said astronomy for non-majors is an easy A, and they were right.
examples.zh: 大家都说非专业的天文课是门「送分课」，事实证明没错。

examples.en: I need one easy A this term to protect my GPA.
examples.zh: 这学期我需要一门能「轻松拿A」的课来保住绩点。

collocations: treat a course as an easy A

words.enDefinition: a comfortably earned B grade, respectable but not spectacular

examples.en: A solid B in thermodynamics will not stop me from graduating with honors.
examples.zh: 热力学拿个「稳稳的B」不会妨碍我以荣誉毕业。

examples.en: I walked out of the final expecting a solid B, not an A minus.
examples.zh: 考完期末我本以为能稳拿个「B」，没想到会是A减。

words.enDefinition: a score right at the edge between two letter grades

examples.en: My 88.4 is a borderline grade, so I emailed the professor about rounding.
examples.zh: 我的88.4分是个「临界成绩」，所以写信问教授能否四舍五入。

examples.en: Borderline grades at the end of term usually go to students with strong participation.
examples.zh: 期末的「边缘成绩」通常判给课堂参与积极的学生。

collocations: a borderline grade between two letters

words.enDefinition: any grade that counts as successfully completing a course

examples.en: You only need a passing grade in the lab to keep your credit.
examples.zh: 实验课只要拿到「合格成绩」就能保住学分。

examples.en: A D is technically a passing grade, but it will drag your GPA down.
examples.zh: D严格来说也算「及格成绩」，但会拖低你的绩点。

words.enDefinition: a grade below the pass line that earns no credit

examples.en: A failing grade in organic chemistry forced me to rethink my pre-med track.
examples.zh: 有机化学的「不及格成绩」让我重新考虑了预医方向。

examples.en: She replaced a failing grade through the grade forgiveness policy last spring.
examples.zh: 去年春天她靠成绩替换政策处理掉了那个「不及格成绩」。

collocations: a failing grade in a required course

words.enDefinition: to pass a course with only the lowest acceptable score

examples.en: I barely passed statistics with a 61, so my GPA took a hit.
examples.zh: 我统计课61分「勉强及格」，绩点受了点影响。

examples.en: He barely passed the lab section but made up for it with an A on the final.
examples.zh: 他实验部分「勉强及格」，但靠期末的A补了回来。

words.enDefinition: a grade of C or higher required for some purpose

examples.en: You need a C or better in chem lab before taking the advanced course.
examples.zh: 先修要求化学实验拿到「C以上」才能选修高级课程。

examples.en: The scholarship renews only for students with a C or better in every class.
examples.zh: 奖学金只延续给每门课都拿到「C或更好」的学生。

collocations: a C or better in the prerequisite

words.enDefinition: the lowest grade accepted for credit, entry, or progression

examples.en: The nursing program sets a minimum grade of B minus in every science course.
examples.zh: 护理项目要求每门理科课的「最低成绩」是B减。

examples.en: Check the catalog for the minimum grade needed to count the elective.
examples.zh: 查一下校规目录里这门选修课计入学位所需的「最低成绩要求」。

words.enDefinition: grades well above average, often used in British universities

examples.en: She earned high marks on every essay in the politics seminar.
examples.zh: 政治研讨课的每篇论文她都拿了「高分」。

examples.en: Consistent high marks across two years made my transcript stand out.
examples.zh: 两年持续拿下「高分」让我的成绩单很出彩。

words.enDefinition: the average of grade points across all courses, shown as a number

examples.en: My grade point average slipped to 2.9 after a rough sophomore year.
examples.zh: 大二不顺之后，我的「平均绩点」掉到了2.9。

examples.en: Most graduate programs list a 3.0 grade point average as the minimum.
examples.zh: 大多数研究生项目把「平均绩点」3.0列为最低线。

words.enDefinition: your overall GPA across every term attended so far

examples.en: The letter says my cumulative GPA must stay above 2.0 to keep financial aid.
examples.zh: 信上说我的「累计绩点」必须保持在2.0以上才能保留助学金。

examples.en: A strong junior year pulled her cumulative GPA back up to 3.4.
examples.zh: 大三的强势表现把她的「累计绩点」拉回3.4。

words.enDefinition: the GPA calculated only from courses in your major

examples.en: My overall GPA is 3.2, but my major GPA is a solid 3.6.
examples.zh: 我的总绩点是3.2，但「专业课绩点」有稳稳的3.6。

examples.en: The honors committee looks at your major GPA, not your electives.
examples.zh: 荣誉评定委员会看的是「专业绩点」，不是选修课。

words.enDefinition: the GPA from science courses, tracked for medical school applications

examples.en: Medical schools weigh your science GPA more than your overall one.
examples.zh: 医学院看「理科绩点」比看总绩点更重。

examples.en: Retaking gen chem lifted my science GPA from 3.0 to 3.4.
examples.zh: 重修普通化学把我的「理科绩点」从3.0提到了3.4。

words.enDefinition: the GPA earned within a single term on its own

examples.en: My semester GPA was 3.8, though my cumulative is still 3.3.
examples.zh: 我这学期「学期绩点」3.8，不过累计的还是3.3。

examples.en: One 2.4 semester GPA barely dented the cumulative I had built up.
examples.zh: 一个2.4的「学期绩点」几乎没撼动我攒起来的累计绩点。

words.enDefinition: a GPA that gives courses different influence by credit hours

examples.en: Weighted GPA favors students who take more credit hours of hard courses.
examples.zh: 「加权绩点」更偏向选修高学分难课的学生。

examples.en: The registrar's office publishes how it computes your weighted GPA each term.
examples.zh: 教务处公布每学期「加权绩点」的计算方法。

words.enDefinition: a plain GPA where every course counts the same

examples.en: My unweighted GPA is 3.0, but weighted it climbs to 3.4.
examples.zh: 我的「非加权绩点」是3.0，加权后升到3.4。

examples.en: Some scholarships ask for the unweighted GPA exactly as printed on the transcript.
examples.zh: 有些奖学金要求填报成绩单上原样的「非加权绩点」。

words.enDefinition: the GPA covering only courses taken at your current school

examples.en: Transfer credits count for graduation but not for my institutional GPA.
examples.zh: 转学分算毕业学分，但不计入我的「本校绩点」。

examples.en: The registrar distinguishes between institutional GPA and cumulative GPA on the audit.
examples.zh: 教务系统在学程审核里区分「本校绩点」和累计绩点。

words.enDefinition: the numerical value a letter grade converts to per credit

examples.en: Most universities assign 4.0 grade points per credit hour for an A.
examples.zh: 多数大学里A折合每学分4.0个「等级点数」。

examples.en: Multiply each course's grade points by its credits, then add them up.
examples.zh: 把每门课的「等级点数」乘以学分，再全部相加。

words.enDefinition: total grade points accumulated across all completed courses

examples.en: Grade points earned divided by credits attempted gives your GPA.
examples.zh: 用「所获绩点」除以修读学分，就得到你的GPA。

examples.en: The unofficial transcript lists grade points earned for every completed term.
examples.zh: 非官方成绩单逐学期列出「所获绩点」。

collocations: divide grade points earned by credits

words.enDefinition: the process of turning grades and credits into a GPA

examples.en: The registrar's website has a worksheet that explains GPA calculation step by step.
examples.zh: 教务处网站有一份工作表，逐步解释「绩点计算」。

examples.en: Repeated courses follow a special rule in the university's GPA calculation.
examples.zh: 重修课程在学校「绩点计算」中遵循特殊规则。

words.enDefinition: an online tool that estimates your GPA from expected grades

examples.en: I ran the GPA calculator with straight A's to see if 3.5 was reachable.
examples.zh: 我在「绩点计算器」里按全A试了试，看3.5够不够得着。

examples.en: The advising office links a GPA calculator for planning next semester's target.
examples.zh: 辅导办公室挂了个「绩点计算器」链接，用来规划下学期目标。

collocations: run the numbers through a GPA calculator

words.enDefinition: the common American grading scale whose top value is 4.0

examples.en: American transcripts report grades on a 4.0 scale, so 3.7 is excellent.
examples.zh: 美国成绩单按「4.0绩点制」报告，所以3.7已经很优秀。

examples.en: My home university uses percentages, so I had to convert to the 4.0 scale.
examples.zh: 我本科学校用百分制，所以必须换算成「4.0绩点制」。

words.enDefinition: a system awarding grades like B plus and C minus

examples.en: Plus/minus grading means an 89 is a B plus, worth only 3.3.
examples.zh: 「加减等级制」意味着89分是B加，只值3.3绩点。

examples.en: Our school switched to plus/minus grading two years ago, and GPAs dipped.
examples.zh: 学校两年前改用「加减等级制」，大家的绩点都降了一点。

words.enDefinition: an average where components count for different percentages

examples.en: Your course grade is a weighted average, with the final worth forty percent.
examples.zh: 你的单科成绩是「加权平均」，期末占四成。

examples.en: The weighted average of my quiz scores pulled the lab grade down.
examples.zh: 我小测分数的「加权平均」把实验成绩拉低了。

words.enDefinition: a grade expressed as a number rather than a letter

examples.en: The portal shows a numeric grade until the registrar converts it to letters.
examples.zh: 系统先显示「数字成绩」，之后教务处才换算成字母等级。

examples.en: A 78 numeric grade sits right at the edge of a C plus.
examples.zh: 78分的「数字成绩」正卡在C加的边缘。

words.enDefinition: the final grade recorded for one complete course

examples.en: Your course grade combines homework, labs, and the final into one letter.
examples.zh: 你的「单科成绩」把作业、实验和期末合成一个等级。

examples.en: An incomplete stays on record until the course grade is finalized.
examples.zh: 未完成成绩会留在档案里，直到「课程成绩」确定为止。

words.enDefinition: the grade you are earning in a course right now

examples.en: Check your current grade before deciding whether to withdraw from economics.
examples.zh: 决定是否退掉经济课前，先看看「当前成绩」。

examples.en: My current grade in bio is 74, so the final really matters.
examples.zh: 生物课我的「当前成绩」是74分，期末就非常关键了。

words.enDefinition: the grade you are likely to receive by term's end

examples.en: With two A's on the midterms, my projected grade is a solid B plus.
examples.zh: 两次期中都拿了A，我的「预估成绩」是稳稳的B加。

examples.en: The syllabus shows how to compute your projected grade before the final.
examples.zh: 课程大纲教你在期末前怎么算「预估成绩」。

words.enDefinition: a tool that estimates your final grade from current scores

examples.en: The grade predictor says I need an 82 on the final for an A minus.
examples.zh: 「成绩预测工具」显示我期末要考82分才能拿A减。

examples.en: Our LMS has a grade predictor built into the grades page.
examples.zh: 我们的学习系统在成绩页面自带「成绩预测器」。

words.enDefinition: a spreadsheet or app for logging scores during the term

examples.en: I keep a grade tracker so nothing surprises me at the end of term.
examples.zh: 我一直用「成绩记录表」，免得期末被分数吓一跳。

examples.en: My grade tracker says I can still pull the chemistry grade to a B.
examples.zh: 我的「成绩追踪表」显示化学成绩还能拉到B。

words.enDefinition: changing grades from one national system into another scale

examples.en: Graduate schools request a GPA conversion for transcripts issued overseas.
examples.zh: 研究生院要求对海外成绩单做「绩点换算」。

examples.en: Use the official chart for GPA conversion, since WES rounds differently.
examples.zh: 做「绩点换算」要用官方对照表，因为WES的取整方式不同。

words.enDefinition: a grading system where the maximum score is 100

examples.en: My Chinese university grades on a 100-point scale, so 85 is strong there.
examples.zh: 我在中国的大学按「百分制」打分，85分在当地已经很好。

examples.en: Admissions offices can translate a 100-point scale into a 4.0 GPA.
examples.zh: 招生办能把「百分制」换算成4.0的GPA。

words.enDefinition: the GPA you type into an application before transcripts arrive

examples.en: Enter your self-reported GPA carefully, because it must match the transcript later.
examples.zh: 填报「自报绩点」要仔细，之后必须和成绩单对得上。

examples.en: My self-reported GPA was 3.42, rounded from the official transcript number.
examples.zh: 我的「自报绩点」是3.42，由成绩单上的官方数字四舍五入而来。

words.enDefinition: the minimum GPA an application or program will consider

examples.en: The department's GPA cutoff for funded spots is 3.5 this year.
examples.zh: 该系有奖学金名额的「绩点门槛」今年是3.5。

examples.en: Missing the GPA cutoff by 0.02 still feels brutal in March.
examples.zh: 差0.02没过「绩点线」，三月份想起来还是很难受。

words.enDefinition: the shortfall when your cumulative GPA falls below the required level

examples.en: After two failed courses I am carrying a GPA deficit of 0.3.
examples.zh: 挂了两门课之后，我身上背着0.3的「绩点亏空」。

examples.en: Clearing the GPA deficit means retaking the courses with D's or F's.
examples.zh: 清除「绩点亏空」的办法就是重修拿了D或F的课。

words.enDefinition: a grade average below what programs or employers expect

examples.en: A low GPA does not end your grad school plans if the rest is strong.
examples.zh: 只要其他条件够硬，「低绩点」并不意味着研究生梦碎。

examples.en: The advisor helped me frame my low GPA as an upward trend story.
examples.zh: 导师帮我把「偏低绩点」讲成了逐步上升的故事。

collocations: a low GPA in freshman year

words.enDefinition: to improve your grade average over later terms

examples.en: Two elective credits in music appreciation helped raise my GPA by 0.1.
examples.zh: 选了两学分的音乐欣赏，帮我把「绩点拉高」了0.1。

examples.en: Retaking the stats course is the fastest way to raise your GPA this year.
examples.zh: 重修统计课是今年「拉高绩点」最快的办法。

words.enDefinition: to earn better marks than you did before

examples.en: Office hours every week is the simplest way to improve your grades.
examples.zh: 每周去答疑时间是最简单的「提高成绩」的办法。

examples.en: After the academic warning, she made a real plan to improve her grades.
examples.zh: 收到学业警告后，她认真做了套「提高成绩」的计划。

words.enDefinition: to damage your grade average severely in one term

examples.en: Overloading eighteen credits can tank your GPA if you also work nights.
examples.zh: 如果晚上还打工，修满18个学分可能「拖垮绩点」。

examples.en: One failed lab course won't tank your GPA if you retake it promptly.
examples.zh: 实验课挂一科，只要及时重修，就不会「拖垮绩点」。

collocations: tank your GPA in one semester
worried it would tank your GPA

words.enDefinition: to be included when your grade average is computed

examples.en: Pass/fail courses do not count toward your GPA, only your credits.
examples.zh: 按合格制修的课不「计入绩点」，只算学分。

examples.en: Repeated courses sometimes count toward your GPA twice under older policies.
examples.zh: 按老政策，重修的课有时会两次「计入绩点」。

collocations: courses that count toward your GPA

words.enDefinition: the effect a single grade has on your average

examples.en: A three-credit elective has a small GPA impact compared to a core course.
examples.zh: 和核心课相比，三学分选修对「绩点的影响」很小。

examples.en: Before switching to pass/fail, students weigh the GPA impact of a likely C.
examples.zh: 改合格制之前，学生会权衡可能拿C对「绩点的影响」。

collocations: the GPA impact of one course

words.enDefinition: a short-term drop in your grade average

examples.en: A one-semester GPA dip rarely sinks a graduate application on its own.
examples.zh: 单学期的「绩点下滑」很少单凭这一点毁掉研究生申请。

examples.en: Explain the GPA dip in your personal statement, since committees understand illness.
examples.zh: 在个人陈述里解释「绩点下滑」的原因，招生官能理解生病的情况。

words.enDefinition: a scheme marking courses only as pass or fail

examples.en: Under pass/fail grading, the transcript shows a P instead of a letter.
examples.zh: 在「合格制计分」下，成绩单上显示P而不是字母等级。

examples.en: Pass/fail grading shields your GPA, but grad schools sometimes prefer letter grades.
examples.zh: 「合格/不及格制」保护绩点，但研究生院有时更想看字母等级。

words.enDefinition: to change a course's grading scheme to pass or fail

examples.en: You can switch to pass/fail until the midpoint of the semester.
examples.zh: 学期过半之前你都可以「改为合格制」。

examples.en: I switched to pass/fail in philosophy after the second midterm disaster.
examples.zh: 第二次期中考砸之后，我把哲学课「换成合格制」了。

collocations: switch to pass/fail before the deadline
switch to pass/fail for one elective

words.enDefinition: the field recording whether a course is graded, pass/fail, or audit

examples.en: The portal lists your grade mode for each class: graded, pass/fail, or audit.
examples.zh: 系统里列出了每门课的「计分模式」：等级制、合格制还是旁听。

examples.en: Changing your grade mode after the deadline requires a petition.
examples.zh: 截止日期后想改「计分模式」就得提交特批申请。

collocations: grade mode of graded or pass/fail

words.enDefinition: the withdrawal mark recorded when you drop a course late

examples.en: A grade of W appears on my transcript but does not touch my GPA.
examples.zh: 我的成绩单上有一个「退课W标记」，但不影响绩点。

examples.en: Two grades of W in one term raised a flag with my advisor.
examples.zh: 一学期两个「W退课标记」引起了导师的注意。

collocations: a grade of W on the transcript

words.enDefinition: a transcript mark that neither adds to nor lowers your GPA

examples.en: A W is a non-punitive grade, so it leaves your GPA untouched.
examples.zh: W属于「非惩罚性成绩」，不会动你的绩点。

examples.en: Incomplete turns punitive if you never finish, so read the non-punitive grade rules.
examples.zh: 未完成成绩拖着不补会变成惩罚性的，所以要读读「非惩罚性成绩」的规定。

words.enDefinition: to arrange extra time to finish a course's remaining work

examples.en: I asked to take an incomplete after mononucleosis wrecked my exam schedule.
examples.zh: 单核细胞增多症打乱了我的考试安排，我申请了「未完成成绩」。

examples.en: Professors usually approve taking an incomplete only with documented emergencies.
examples.zh: 教授通常只对有证明的紧急情况批准「办理未完成成绩」。

collocations: take an incomplete in a course

words.enDefinition: to finish outstanding work so a temporary grade becomes final

examples.en: You have until March to resolve an incomplete before it lapses to an F.
examples.zh: 你要在三月前「补完未完成成绩」，否则会自动记F。

examples.en: She resolved the incomplete by submitting the missed lab reports in January.
examples.zh: 她一月份补交了缺的实验报告，「了结了缓评」。

collocations: resolve an incomplete by the deadline
resolve an incomplete with the professor

words.enDefinition: a course taken again to improve an earlier grade

examples.en: Only the higher grade of a repeated course enters the GPA calculation.
examples.zh: 「重修课程」只把更高的那次成绩计入绩点计算。

examples.en: My transcript marks the repeated course with an R flag.
examples.zh: 我的成绩单给「重修课程」标了R记号。

collocations: a repeated course on the transcript

words.enDefinition: credits for courses you are taking but have not finished

examples.en: In-progress credits show on the audit but not in the GPA yet.
examples.zh: 「进行中学分」会出现在审核单上，但还没进绩点。

examples.en: Add your in-progress credits when planning whether a heavy semester is safe.
examples.zh: 规划这一学期强度是否安全时，要把「进行中学分」算进去。

collocations: in-progress credits on the degree audit

words.enDefinition: to adjust exam scores upward relative to the class average

examples.en: The professor promised to curve an exam if the class median fell below 65.
examples.zh: 教授承诺如果「班级中位数」低于65就给考试调分。

examples.en: They curved the midterm by adding six points to every raw score.
examples.zh: 期中考试时老师按「调分」给每份卷子加了6分。

words.enDefinition: a grade raised or set after a class-wide adjustment

examples.en: My curved grade in orgo jumped from a 68 to a B minus.
examples.zh: 有机化学「调分后成绩」从68分跳到了B减。

examples.en: The registrar posts curved grades only after the department signs off.
examples.zh: 「调分后成绩」要等系里签字后才发布。

collocations: a curved grade on the midterm

words.enDefinition: an official change made to a posted score or letter

examples.en: The curve was a five-point grade adjustment for the whole section.
examples.zh: 这次「成绩调整」是给整个小班统一加5分。

examples.en: Ask about a grade adjustment only if the points were actually miscounted.
examples.zh: 只有在分数确实算错时才去申请「成绩调整」。

words.enDefinition: to score highest and become the benchmark for class scaling
acceptedEnVariants: set the curve on the exam

examples.en: Kevin set the curve on the orgo midterm with a 98.
examples.zh: 凯文有机化学期中考了98分，「定下了曲线基准」。

examples.en: Nobody has set the curve in this weeder class for three semesters.
examples.zh: 这门筛选课已经三个学期没人「定下曲线基准」了。

collocations: set the curve on the midterm
the student who set the curve

words.enDefinition: a policy limiting how many students may earn each grade

examples.en: Law schools use a forced curve, so only a set share earn A's.
examples.zh: 法学院实行「强制曲线分布」，只有固定比例的人能拿A。

examples.en: Under the forced curve, my 91 became a B plus instead of an A.
examples.zh: 在「强制曲线」下，我的91分只能算B加而不是A。

words.enDefinition: a small raise in a grade from scaling or rounding

examples.en: The curve gave everyone a two-point grade bump before posting.
examples.zh: 出分前，曲线让每人的分数都有了一点「上调」。

examples.en: Rounding my 79.5 gave a one-letter grade bump to a B.
examples.zh: 79.5四舍五入后让我的等级「上调了一档」，变成了B。

words.enDefinition: the middle score of the whole class on an assessment

examples.en: The class median on the bio final was 71, so the professor curved it.
examples.zh: 生物期末的「班级中位数」是71分，教授因此调了分。

examples.en: Comparing your score to the class median beats guessing from the raw number.
examples.zh: 把你的分数和「全班中位数」比一比，比盯着原始分瞎猜强。

collocations: curve based on the class median

words.enDefinition: the itemized parts that add up to your course grade

examples.en: The grade breakdown on the syllabus lists homework at twenty percent.
examples.zh: 课程大纲上的「成绩构成」写着作业占20%。

examples.en: I misread the grade breakdown and thought the final was optional.
examples.zh: 我看错了「分数构成」，以为期末考是选考的。

collocations: the grade breakdown in the syllabus

words.enDefinition: the trend of average grades rising higher over time

examples.en: Grade inflation means a B today would have been a C a generation ago.
examples.zh: 「分数通胀」意味着今天的B相当于上一代人的C。

examples.en: Admissions officers adjust for grade inflation when comparing applicants from different schools.
examples.zh: 招生官比较不同学校申请者时会校正「分数通胀」因素。

collocations: a school known for grade inflation

words.enDefinition: a policy or culture of keeping average grades low

examples.en: That department is famous for grade deflation, so a B there means a lot.
examples.zh: 那个系以「压分」出名，所以在那儿拿B含金量很高。

examples.en: Graduate committees note grade deflation when they read transcripts from certain schools.
examples.zh: 研究生委员会看到某些学校的成绩单时会考虑「分数紧缩」的情况。

words.enDefinition: a grouped set of assignments like quizzes or labs in the gradebook

examples.en: The gradebook shows each grade category with its weight for the final.
examples.zh: 在线记分册显示每个「成绩类别」及其在期末的权重。

examples.en: Drop the lowest score within each grade category before averaging.
examples.zh: 平均之前，每个「计分类别」里先去掉最低分。

collocations: drop the lowest in a grade category

words.enDefinition: how many points an assignment is worth in total

examples.en: Check the point value before skipping a small homework set.
examples.zh: 放弃某次小作业前，先看看它的「分值」。

examples.en: The final project has a point value of 200, a third of the course.
examples.zh: 期末项目的「分值」是200分，占整门课的三分之一。

collocations: the point value of an assignment

words.enDefinition: all points available across a course's assignments

examples.en: There are 1,000 total points in this class, and the final is 300.
examples.zh: 这门课「总点数」是1000，期末占300。

examples.en: I added my scores and divided by the total points to get 84 percent.
examples.zh: 我把得分加起来除以「总点数」，得到84%。

words.enDefinition: to ignore your worst score when averaging the rest

examples.en: The professor drops the lowest grade among the ten quizzes.
examples.zh: 教授会在十次小测里「去掉最低分」。

examples.en: Dropping the lowest grade saved my semester average twice this year.
examples.zh: 今年「去掉最低分」两次救了我的学期平均分。

collocations: policy of dropping the lowest grade
drop the lowest grade before averaging

words.enDefinition: bumping a score up to the next letter at a threshold

examples.en: The syllabus explicitly says there is no grade rounding at term's end.
examples.zh: 课程大纲明确写了期末「不做成绩四舍五入」。

examples.en: Some professors practice grade rounding for averages within 0.5 of a letter.
examples.zh: 有些教授会对离等级线不到0.5分的平均分做「成绩取整」。

words.enDefinition: the official rules for how a course's grades are assigned

examples.en: The grading policy in the syllabus explains late penalties and regrades.
examples.zh: 课程大纲里的「评分政策」解释了迟交罚分和重判规则。

examples.en: Department-wide grading policy keeps two sections of the same course comparable.
examples.zh: 全系统一的「评分政策」让同一门课的不同班可比。

words.enDefinition: the exact calculation that produces the course grade

examples.en: The grading formula weights the final at forty percent of the course.
examples.zh: 「计分公式」把期末权重设为整门课的40%。

examples.en: Plug your scores into the grading formula to estimate your final letter.
examples.zh: 把你的分数代入「计分公式」，就能估算出期末等级。

collocations: the grading formula in the syllabus

words.enDefinition: marking student work without seeing names attached to it

examples.en: Anonymous grading on the philosophy essays removes any favoritism worries.
examples.zh: 哲学论文采用「匿名评分」，免除了偏心的顾虑。

examples.en: The department introduced anonymous grading after complaints about inconsistent marking.
examples.zh: 在有评分不一的投诉之后，系里推行了「匿名评分」。

words.enDefinition: all credit hours you have enrolled in, finished or not

examples.en: Your GPA equals grade points earned divided by credits attempted each term.
examples.zh: 你的GPA等于所获绩点除以每学期的「修读学分」。

examples.en: Withdrawn courses still count in credits attempted but earn no grade points.
examples.zh: 退掉的课仍计入「修读学分」，但不产生等级点数。

words.enDefinition: credit hours successfully completed with passing grades

examples.en: Pass/fail courses with a P still add credits earned toward graduation.
examples.zh: 合格制课程拿到P照样「修得学分」，计入毕业要求。

examples.en: The degree audit compares credits earned against the 120-credit requirement.
examples.zh: 学程审核把「修得学分」和120学分的毕业要求作对比。

words.enDefinition: to ask a professor to explain or review a posted grade

examples.en: Email the TA first if you want to question a grade on the problem set.
examples.zh: 如果你想「质疑习题集的分数」，先给助教发邮件。

examples.en: Most students question a grade politely and get the mistake fixed in a day.
examples.zh: 多数学生礼貌地「对成绩提出疑问」，一天内就能改好。

words.enDefinition: to formally ask for your exam to be marked again

examples.en: You can request a regrade within one week of the score release.
examples.zh: 出分后一周内可以「申请重新判分」。

examples.en: I requested a regrade because the rubric line about diagrams was skipped.
examples.zh: 我「申请了重判」，因为评分标准里有关图示的那条被漏看了。

collocations: request a regrade within a week
request a regrade through the form
request a regrade for one question

words.enDefinition: a formal disagreement between a student and a posted grade

examples.en: A grade dispute starts with the instructor and escalates to the department.
examples.zh: 「成绩争议」先找任课老师解决，解决不了再升级到系里。

examples.en: He filed a grade dispute over the group project's individual scores.
examples.zh: 他就小组项目里的个人得分提交了「成绩争议」。

collocations: a grade dispute over the final

words.enDefinition: the form an instructor files to correct a posted grade

examples.en: The professor submitted a grade change form after finding the addition error.
examples.zh: 教授发现加总错误后提交了「改分申请表」。

examples.en: A grade change form goes through the registrar, not through the portal.
examples.zh: 「成绩更改表」走教务处流程，不走学生系统。

collocations: a grade change form after regrading

words.enDefinition: a mismatch between your records and the posted grade

examples.en: I found a grade discrepancy between my points sheet and the portal.
examples.zh: 我发现我的记分表和系统之间有「成绩出入」。

examples.en: Report any grade discrepancy to the TA with screenshots attached.
examples.zh: 发现「分数不符」就截图向助教报告。

collocations: a grade discrepancy of five points

words.enDefinition: the moment final grades appear in the student system

examples.en: Grade posting for fall term starts December 22 at noon.
examples.zh: 秋季学期「成绩发布」从12月22日中午开始。

examples.en: Delays in grade posting usually mean the registrar is processing incompletes.
examples.zh: 「成绩发布」延迟通常意味着教务处还在处理缓评。

collocations: grade posting in the student portal

words.enDefinition: an end-of-term summary of the grades you received

examples.en: The grade report emails out a week after finals end.
examples.zh: 「成绩通知单」在期末考试结束一周后邮件发出。

examples.en: My parents asked for a copy of the semester grade report.
examples.zh: 我父母要了一份学期「成绩报告单」的副本。

words.enDefinition: the process of instructors uploading final grades to the registrar

examples.en: Grade submission closes within forty-eight hours after each final exam ends.
examples.zh: 每场期末考结束后48小时内要完成「成绩提交」。

examples.en: Late grade submission is why my transcript still shows an empty column.
examples.zh: 老师「提交成绩」晚了，所以我的成绩单那栏还空着。

words.enDefinition: to look up your posted scores in the student portal

examples.en: Check your grades tonight; the registrar said posting begins at five.
examples.zh: 今晚记得「查成绩」，教务处说五点开始出分。

examples.en: I check my grades weekly so nothing on the transcript ever surprises me.
examples.zh: 我每周都「查看成绩」，免得成绩单上出现意外。

collocations: check your grades after each quiz

words.enDefinition: a blank where a course grade should appear on record

examples.en: There's a missing grade for my statistics lab on the portal.
examples.zh: 系统里我统计实验课的「成绩缺失」了。

examples.en: Email the professor immediately about the missing grade before it delays graduation clearance.
examples.zh: 赶紧给教授发邮件说明「缺失的成绩」，免得拖慢毕业审核。

collocations: a missing grade on the transcript

words.enDefinition: the online record of scores for every assignment in a course

examples.en: The online gradebook updates overnight after the TAs finish marking each week.
examples.zh: 助教每周批改完，网上「记分册」隔夜就会更新。

examples.en: Check the gradebook before the withdrawal deadline so nothing catches you off guard.
examples.zh: 退课截止前先看看「在线成绩册」，免得措手不及。

words.enDefinition: an automatic message telling you a new grade is posted

examples.en: I set up grade notifications so each posted score lands in my inbox.
examples.zh: 我设置了「成绩通知」，每次出分都会进我的邮箱。

examples.en: Turn off grade notifications during finals week if they make you anxious.
examples.zh: 如果让你焦虑，期末周就把「出分提醒」关掉。

words.enDefinition: your complete term-by-term list of grades in one view

examples.en: The portal's grade history page shows every term since freshman year.
examples.zh: 系统的「成绩记录」页显示大一以来的每个学期。

examples.en: Scrolling through my grade history, I watched the upward trend after sophomore year.
examples.zh: 翻看「历史成绩」，能看到大二之后明显的上升趋势。

words.enDefinition: an early-term grade showing whether you are on track

examples.en: First-year students receive progress grades at the midpoint of every fall term.
examples.zh: 大一学生每学期中段会收到「阶段成绩」。

examples.en: A low progress grade triggers a meeting with your academic advisor.
examples.zh: 「进度成绩」太低会触发和学业导师的约谈。

words.enDefinition: a policy that removes old grades from your GPA calculation

examples.en: Academic renewal let me exclude my failed courses from ten years ago.
examples.zh: 「旧成绩重置」政策让我排除了十年前挂掉的课。

examples.en: Ask the registrar whether academic renewal applies to returning adult students.
examples.zh: 问问教务处「学业重新起算」是否适用于回归的成人学生。

collocations: academic renewal after a long break

words.enDefinition: the announced day final grades become visible to students

examples.en: The grade release date for spring term is May 16.
examples.zh: 春季学期「成绩公布日」是5月16日。

examples.en: Circle the grade release date, because transcript requests spike right after it.
examples.zh: 在日历上圈出「出分日期」，之后开成绩单证明的人会暴增。

words.enDefinition: the official note marking a degree earned with honors

examples.en: The honors designation prints on both the diploma and the transcript.
examples.zh: 「荣誉标注」会同时印在毕业证和成绩单上。

examples.en: You need a 3.6 to keep the honors designation through graduation.
examples.zh: 要保住「荣誉标注」直到毕业，绩点得达到3.6。

collocations: an honors designation on the diploma

words.enDefinition: a top honors level awarded for very strong grades

examples.en: She graduated with high honors after two years on the dean's list.
examples.zh: 连续两年上优秀生名单后，她以「优等荣誉」毕业。

examples.en: The department awards high honors only to the top five percent.
examples.zh: 该系只给排名前5%的学生授予「优等荣誉」。

words.enDefinition: the topmost honors level, above high honors

examples.en: A 3.9 cumulative GPA put him in range for highest honors.
examples.zh: 3.9的累计绩点让他够到了「最高荣誉」的范围。

examples.en: She finished with highest honors and a published thesis chapter.
examples.zh: 她以「最高荣誉」毕业，还发表了一章论文。

words.enDefinition: honors granted by your major department for excellence

examples.en: Departmental honors in economics required a thesis and a 3.7 major GPA.
examples.zh: 经济学「系荣誉」要求提交论文且专业绩点3.7。

examples.en: Apply for departmental honors through your advisor by junior year.
examples.zh: 想申请「院系荣誉」，大三前就要通过导师报名。

words.enDefinition: the grade level required to qualify for honors recognition

examples.en: Honors eligibility usually begins at a 3.5 cumulative GPA or better.
examples.zh: 「荣誉资格」通常从累计绩点3.5起步。

examples.en: Check honors eligibility rules before your final semester, not after.
examples.zh: 查「荣誉评定资格」要在最后一学期之前，别拖到之后。

words.enDefinition: a formal award for outstanding work within your major

examples.en: Distinction in the major appears on the transcript next to your degree.
examples.zh: 「专业方向荣誉」会标注在成绩单的学位旁边。

examples.en: Only twelve students earned distinction in the major this year.
examples.zh: 今年只有12人获得「专业方向荣誉」。

collocations: criteria for distinction in the major
distinction in the major on the diploma

words.enDefinition: to pass a course at an exceptionally high standard

examples.en: She passed with distinction on the honors seminar's final portfolio.
examples.zh: 她在荣誉研讨课的期末作品集上「以优异成绩通过」。

examples.en: Students who pass with distinction get a note added to the transcript.
examples.zh: 「优秀通过」的学生会在成绩单上加注说明。

collocations: pass with distinction in a seminar
a result of passed with distinction

words.enDefinition: the combined status required for study abroad and internships
acceptedEnVariants: in good academic and disciplinary standing

examples.en: Study abroad applicants must be in good academic and disciplinary standing.
examples.zh: 留学交换申请者必须「学业品行良好」。

examples.en: The internship form asks your dean to confirm good academic and disciplinary standing.
examples.zh: 实习表格需要院长确认你「学业品行都良好」。

collocations: in good academic and disciplinary standing
confirm good academic and disciplinary standing
maintain good academic and disciplinary standing

words.enDefinition: the measurable progress toward a degree that financial aid requires

examples.en: Financial aid continues only while you maintain satisfactory academic progress.
examples.zh: 只有保持「学业进展达标」，助学金才会继续发放。

examples.en: Dropping below satisfactory academic progress puts your aid package on hold.
examples.zh: 一旦低于「学业进度达标」线，你的资助套餐就会被暂停。

words.enDefinition: ongoing worry about scores and their consequences

examples.en: Grade anxiety peaked for me the night before fall grades posted.
examples.zh: 秋季成绩出分前夜，我的「成绩焦虑」达到顶点。

examples.en: Counseling services run workshops on managing grade anxiety each midterm season.
examples.zh: 每逢期中季，心理中心都会开「成绩焦虑」管理工作坊。

words.enDefinition: a score much lower than you hoped for

examples.en: My first bad grade in college was a 58 on the chem midterm.
examples.zh: 我大学第一个「差成绩」是化学期中的58分。

examples.en: One bad grade early in the term still leaves time to recover.
examples.zh: 学期初的一个「差成绩」还留有补救的时间。

collocations: a bad grade on the midterm

words.enDefinition: a grade below what your effort led you to expect

examples.en: After weeks of revising, a disappointing grade on the essay hit hard.
examples.zh: 改了几周稿子，论文却拿到「令人失望的成绩」，挺受打击。

examples.en: She turned the disappointing grade into a regrade request that succeeded.
examples.zh: 她把那次「失望的成绩」变成了成功的重判申请。

collocations: a disappointing grade on the essay

words.enDefinition: the surprise of a first grade far below high school results

examples.en: Grade shock is real when your first college essay returns a C plus.
examples.zh: 大学第一篇论文只拿回C加时，「成绩落差」的冲击是真实的。

examples.en: Most freshmen recover from grade shock by midterms of second semester.
examples.zh: 多数新生到第二学期期中就能走出「成绩落差」。

words.enDefinition: a term whose grades fall well below your usual level

examples.en: One bad semester during Covid does not define your college GPA.
examples.zh: 疫情期间的一个「糟糕学期」并不能定义你的大学绩点。

examples.en: I explained my bad semester in the addendum about my family emergency.
examples.zh: 我在补充说明里解释了因家庭变故导致的那个「糟糕学期」。

words.enDefinition: stress caused by expectations attached to grades

examples.en: Grade pressure from scholarship renewals made every quiz feel final-exam serious.
examples.zh: 奖学金续评带来的「成绩压力」让每次小测都像期末一样沉重。

examples.en: Peer grade pressure fades once you stop comparing transcripts in the group chat.
examples.zh: 不再在群聊里比成绩单后，来自同伴的「分数压力」就淡了。

words.enDefinition: a student who constantly begs for extra points after grading

examples.en: Nobody wants to be the grade grubber who emails after every quiz.
examples.zh: 没人想成为每次小测后都发邮件「抠分的学生」。

examples.en: Even the professor can spot a grade grubber from the first polite complaint.
examples.zh: 连教授都能从第一次客气的申诉里认出「纠缠分数的学生」。

words.enDefinition: an instructor known for awarding lower grades than expected

examples.en: Professor Nguyen is a tough grader, so an A in her seminar means something.
examples.zh: Nguyen教授「给分很严」，所以她研讨课的A含金量很高。

examples.en: Check Rate My Professors to see who is a tough grader before enrolling.
examples.zh: 选课前上评师网站看看哪位是「给分严格的老师」。

words.enDefinition: an instructor known for awarding generous grades

examples.en: Take Doctor Alvarez for the elective; everyone says she is an easy grader.
examples.zh: 选修课选Alvarez博士，大家都说她是「给分宽松的老师」。

examples.en: An easy grader can lift your semester GPA without extra study time.
examples.zh: 遇上「给分松的老师」，不加班加点也能拉高学期绩点。

words.enDefinition: a deliberately hard course that filters out weaker majors

examples.en: Organic chemistry is the classic weed-out course for pre-med students.
examples.zh: 有机化学是预医学生公认的「筛选课」。

examples.en: Surviving the weed-out course felt better than the A itself.
examples.zh: 熬过那门「淘汰课」比拿到A本身还让人有成就感。

collocations: a weed-out course for the major

words.enDefinition: to score below your usual level on an assessment

examples.en: I underperformed on the physics final and finished with a B minus.
examples.zh: 我物理期末「发挥失常」，最后拿了B减。

examples.en: Students who underperform once often rebound strongly on the next assessment.
examples.zh: 一次「发挥失常」的学生常在下次考核强势反弹。

collocations: underperform relative to the class average

words.enDefinition: to rescue a failing course grade before the term ends

examples.en: There is still time to salvage your grade if you ace both remaining labs.
examples.zh: 只要剩下两次实验都拿A，还来得及「挽救成绩」。

examples.en: Extra credit offered at the end helped me salvage my grade in chemistry.
examples.zh: 期末推出的加分项帮我「挽救了化学成绩」。

words.enDefinition: a copying mistake made when grades or credits were recorded

examples.en: A transcription error turned my B into a D on the official record.
examples.zh: 官方记录上的一次「誊录错误」把我的B错登成了D。

examples.en: Report the transcription error to the registrar with your graded exam attached.
examples.zh: 附上批改后的试卷，向教务处报告这处「录入错误」。

collocations: a transcription error on the transcript

words.enDefinition: a second-check process that keeps marking standards consistent

examples.en: British universities use grade moderation to compare marking across markers.
examples.zh: 英国大学用「成绩复核」来统一不同阅卷人的标准。

examples.en: My essay went through grade moderation before the final mark was confirmed.
examples.zh: 我的论文在最终分数确认前经过了「评分复核」。

words.enDefinition: extra points awarded beyond the standard maximum score

examples.en: The bonus points on question twelve saved my statistics grade.
examples.zh: 第12题的「附加分」救了我的统计课成绩。

examples.en: Bonus points cannot push your total above the hundred-percent cap.
examples.zh: 「加分」不能让总分突破百分上限。

words.enDefinition: to lift a weak course grade through later work

examples.en: Two strong problem sets can still pull up your grade before the final.
examples.zh: 两次高质量的习题还能在期末前「把成绩拉上来」。

examples.en: She pulled up her grade from a D plus to a B minus after office hours.
examples.zh: 她靠多去答疑把「成绩拉了上来」，从D加升到B减。

collocations: pull up your grade late in term
pull the grade up to a B
hard to pull up your grade

words.enDefinition: a temporary grade that can still change after review

examples.en: Provisional grades for the module appear online before the exam board meets.
examples.zh: 模块的「暂定成绩」会在考试委员会开会前先上网。

examples.en: Treat the provisional grade as final only after the transcript is issued.
examples.zh: 成绩单签发之前，别把「临时成绩」当成最终结果。

words.enDefinition: the grade average you aim to reach by a deadline

examples.en: Set a target GPA of 3.5 for the year and plan courses backward from it.
examples.zh: 把全年「目标绩点」定为3.5，再倒推排课。

examples.en: My target GPA for graduation is 3.6, so this term I need a 3.7.
examples.zh: 我的毕业「目标绩点」是3.6，所以这学期得拿3.7。

words.enDefinition: a simulated GPA showing outcomes if future grades change

examples.en: The advisor ran a what-if GPA to show how an A in orgo changes everything.
examples.zh: 导师跑了一个「模拟绩点」，展示有机化学拿A能改变什么。

examples.en: Use the what-if GPA tool before deciding to take the hard elective.
examples.zh: 决定选那门硬核选修前，先用「假设绩点」工具算一算。

words.enDefinition: an unusually kind class-wide adjustment to exam scores

examples.en: The orgo final came with a generous curve that lifted many B's into A minus territory.
examples.zh: 有机化学期末的「调分很宽松」，把不少B抬进了A减区间。

examples.en: Do not count on a generous curve; the department has tightened its policy.
examples.zh: 别指望「宽松的曲线」，系里已经收紧了政策。

collocations: a generous curve on the final
the professor gave a generous curve

words.enDefinition: the GPA carried in from a school you attended earlier

examples.en: My transfer GPA from community college reset when I entered the university.
examples.zh: 进入本校后，社区学院的「转入绩点」就清零重算了。

examples.en: Some scholarships combine your transfer GPA with your current institutional GPA.
examples.zh: 有些奖学金会把「转学前绩点」和本校绩点合并计算。

words.enDefinition: your final undergraduate average as reported on applications

examples.en: Graduate admissions weigh junior-year courses most heavily within your college GPA.
examples.zh: 研究生招生在「大学绩点」里最看重大三的课。

examples.en: Her 3.4 college GPA cleared the program's stated cutoff with room to spare.
examples.zh: 她3.4的「本科绩点」稳稳过了项目的明线。

words.enDefinition: all credit hours completed across every term so far

examples.en: The audit shows 96 cumulative credits against the 120 needed to graduate.
examples.zh: 审核单显示我已有96个「累计学分」，毕业需要120个。

examples.en: Cumulative credits, not semesters, decide when you can register as a senior.
examples.zh: 决定你能否按大四优先注册的是「累计学分」，而非学期数。
